## Why Enterprise AI Projects Fail: Diagnosing Execution Over Algorithms
_Audience:_ Enterprise technology leadership outlets and CIO podcasts focused on strategic alignment and operational hurdles in enterprise AI transformations.

- AI initiatives rarely succeed or fail based on algorithms or infrastructure, but rather depend on clarity of purpose, organizational alignment, and disciplined execution. [C5]
- Audits of failed AI projects reveal that root causes consistently stem from poor data quality, unclear objectives, or organizational unreadiness rather than algorithmic limitations. [C6]
- Companies should advance methodically to build strong foundations for sustainable transformation instead of rushing toward advanced adoption stages with fragile quick fixes. [C7]

## Sources (verbatim, verified against the live page)

- **C5** "The difference between AI success and failure rarely comes down to algorithms or infrastructure. It comes down to clarity of purpose, organizational alignment, and disciplined execution." - https://prommer.net/en/tech/guides/ai-strategy/
- **C6** "In every failed AI project I've audited, the root cause was never the algorithm. It was always data quality, unclear objectives, or lack of organizational readiness." - https://prommer.net/en/tech/guides/ai-strategy/
- **C7** "The goal isn't to race to Stage 4—it's to progress deliberately, building the foundations that enable sustainable transformation rather than fragile quick fixes." - https://prommer.net/en/tech/guides/ai-strategy/
